page: Hetzner Cloud cx53 is a virtual server instance within the Cost Optimized family, provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. The system provides 16 shared vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, coupled with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Local storage comprises an integrated 320 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates without a dedicated GPU accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the cx53 primarily in the middle 50% tier across general computing, memory, and database tasks. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 30,149.72 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 4,993.0, with stress-ng recording 42,844.81 in multi-core throughput. Read-only memory bandwidth reached 128.82 GB/sec on uncached large blocks and 1,890.65 GB/sec on cached small blocks. Text-generation inference on a small 135M language model registered in the top 25% at 276.25 tokens per second. However, single-core metrics reflect the shared 2.0 GHz CPU configuration: Geekbench single-core scored 706.0 and text processing scored 685.0, both landing in the bottom 10%.

Positioned within the Cost Optimized tier, the cx53 prioritizes resource density over dedicated CPU frequency, delivering 16 cores and fast local NVMe storage at an economical profile. The trade-off lies in shared CPU scheduling and modest single-thread performance, making it less suitable for latency-critical single-threaded execution. Instead, the configuration is best aligned with multi-threaded, parallelized workloads such as batch data processing, build and CI/CD pipelines, container hosting, static web serving (benchmarked at 22.86 GB/sec), and distributed caching using Redis, where 30.09 million SET operations per second were recorded.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx53 is a cost-optimized x86_64 cloud server offering 16 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz, 31.0 GB of memory, and a 320 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU hardware. Hypervisor virtualization is managed through QEMU. Benchmark evaluations place the server's multi-core and memory capabilities in the median 50% tier, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 30,149.72, stress-ng multi-core performance of 42,844.81, and a Redis throughput of 30.09 million SET operations per second. However, the shared core allocation and modest clock speed lead to poor single-core metrics, with Geekbench single-core in the bottom 10%. With roughly 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU and fast NVMe storage, the cx53 provides high resource density for cost-sensitive multi-threaded tasks, including CI/CD compilation, container clusters, batch processing, and static web serving, while being less suited for single-thread latency-sensitive operations.
